_comment: Allowlist of every Secret Manager secret the TEE may read or write, plus auxiliary metadata for the per-call-site checker. Adding a new secret requires changing both this file and the source AND the matching IAM grants in terraform/main.tf's secrets_needing_read / secrets_needing_write locals. The diff bumps the rules digest so external verifiers can detect drift.
_read_comment: Maps the env-var name the workload exports to the Secret Manager secret name. The `SECRETS` object in src/server.js must mirror this map exactly. Reads from any other secret name fail check-secrets.mjs.
_aux_read_comment: Direct fetchSecret*/value reads that don't flow through the SECRETS map -- e.g. TLS cert/key on startup, the persistent ACME account key. The `file` field pins WHERE the call may originate so a future contributor can't add `fetchSecretByName('auth-broker-tls-key')` from an unrelated module.
_write_comment: writeSecretValue call sites. The ACME renewal flow in src/tls.js rotates the TLS material; the persistent ACME account key is sealed once on first run from src/acme-account.js. Every entry MUST set `file`.
_callsite_check_excludes_comment: Files where the per-call-site checker is suppressed because they define Secret Manager helper functions and necessarily trampoline dynamic arguments internally. Do NOT list callers like src/server.js here; use validated_secret_loader_calls for narrow audited dynamic-loader patterns.
_validated_secret_loader_calls_comment: Narrow dynamic-call exceptions whose reachable secret names are already pinned by the SECRETS object above. The checker verifies the call is inside the named function, inside map_source.map(...), that the callback binds the configured array value parameter, and that map_source is initialized from Object.entries(validated_map).
_env_var_allowlist_comment: process.env.X reads where X matches the token-like regex are checked against this list. Names here are env-var keys exported by the TEE (mostly the keys of `read` above) plus operational config. Adding a sneak `process.env.SNUCK_IN_API_KEY` read fails the check until both this allowlist and the source agree.
_env_var_token_regex_comment: Regex applied (case-insensitive) to env-var names. Matches anything containing token / secret / key / credential / password / hmac / api_key. Anything matching that the source reads but is NOT in env_var_allowlist above fails the check.
